Manage and refer urgently:
If shock/SBP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
DIZZINESS
1If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 2One drink is 1 tot of spirits, or 1 small glass (125mL) of wine or 1 can/bottle (330mL) of beer.

Approach to the patient with dizziness not needing urgent attention • Ask about ear symptoms, if present 50. If hearing loss, refer same week. • Ask about fainting/collapse attacks. If present, do ECG. If ECG abnormal, refer same day. • Screen for substance use: in the past year, has patient drunk ≥ 4 drinks2/session, used illegal drugs or misused prescription/over-the-counter medications? If yes to any 165. • Review medication: fluoxetine, hypertension and antiseizure medication, furosemide and efavirenz can cause dizziness. Discuss with doctor. • Check Hb: if < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), anaemia likely 44. • Check BP: if ≥ 140/90 148. Measure BP after lying for 5 minutes and repeat again after standing for 3 minutes. Does systolic BP drop by ≥ 20 or diastolic BP drop by ≥ 10?
• If none of the above, check TSH. If abnormal, refer to doctor. • Refer if no cause is found, dizziness persists despite above treatment or uncertain of diagnosis.
Yes

Orthostatic hypotension likely • Common in the elderly. • If diarrhoea 58, if vomiting 57, if fever 38. If poor fluid intake, encourage fluids and give oral rehydration solution. • Advise patient to sit first before standing up from lying down.
Was patient breathing very quickly or deeply immediately before or during the collapse?

Hyperventilation likely • May also have light- headedness, chest tightness, tingling of hands/feet and visual changes. Usually with emotional stress. • Encourage to breathe at a normal rate and depth. • Assess for stress and anxiety 98. • If recurrent episodes, refer to psychologist.
Sudden dizziness lasting seconds, precipitated by head movements

Positional vertigo likely • Reassure patient that dizziness is self-limiting and usually resolves within 6 months. • If no neck or heart problems, doctor to perform particle repositioning (Epley) manoeuvre. • If headaches, visual symptoms or hearing loss/tinnitus develop, refer.

with nausea/vomiting. May have

Refer.
Vestibular neuronitis likely • Mobilise as soon as possible. • If hearing loss/tinnitus develop or no better after 2 weeks, refer.
Ask about associated symptoms and length of dizziness. Is there hearing loss or tinnitus (ringing/buzzing in ear/s)?
